policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders 'at the two ends thereof' — a plural noun with a singular possessive suffix, which both readings supply. The qere קְצוֹתָיו and the ketiv קצוותו are orthographic variants of the same plural 'its ends'; neither adds, drops, or changes a word the English could show, and no ASV note is mapped here. Underdetermined; the qere base fallback carries the projection.
